passage: Noor noticed that Thomas, the new junior designer, had started carrying the same green notebook she did, drinking her kind of black tea, and even ending emails with her habit of "Let me know if this works". It amused her, and it also made her uneasy. On Thursday, Thomas asked how she had got such a clean client sign-off. Noor hesitated. "That one nearly fell apart," she said. "I missed two deadlines and hid it for a week before telling my boss. I wouldn't do it that way again." Thomas blinked. "I thought you never messed up." "I mess up a lot," Noor said. "Take the parts of me worth copying, not that part." Thomas wrote something in the green notebook.

qa.q: What did Thomas start carrying that matched Noor's?
qa.a: Thomas started carrying the same green notebook as Noor.

qa.q: Why did Noor feel both amused and uneasy about Thomas copying her?
qa.a: It was flattering but also a responsibility, since Thomas might copy her bad habits and see her as someone who never makes mistakes.

qa.q: How did Noor handle being looked up to?
qa.a: She told the truth about how the sign-off nearly fell apart, including the missed deadlines and hiding it, instead of letting Thomas admire a spotless image.

qa.q: What might Thomas have believed about Noor before that talk?
qa.a: That Noor never made mistakes, as the surprise in "I thought you never messed up" suggests.

grounding: A younger colleague copies Noor's habits; she treats it as an honour and responsibility and is honest about her failure.

passage:
Dilnaz: Ganga didi, can I ask how you plan your week? I want to do it exactly like you
Ganga: 😅 exactly like me?
Dilnaz: yes! the colour-coded calendar, the 6am gym, the way you talk to clients. You're my role model
Ganga: that's really kind. and a bit scary
Ganga: can I be honest? last month I messed up the Sharma account. I promised a deadline I couldn't meet and had to apologise
Dilnaz: you?? 😮
Ganga: me. and the 6am gym happens maybe twice a week
Ganga: copy the good bits. like telling clients the truth even when it's awkward. not the calendar
Dilnaz: ok but you're still my role model
Ganga: I'll take it. but find your own way of working too. you're good at things I'm not
Dilnaz: like what
Ganga: you remember every client's kid's name. I don't
Dilnaz: 🥹
Ganga: see you tomorrow. bring your plan and we'll make it yours

qa.q: Which account did Ganga mess up?
How does Ganga feel about Dilnaz wanting to copy her exactly?
qa.a: Ganga feels touched and honoured, but also a little uneasy, calling it "a bit scary".

qa.q: What did Ganga do to use Dilnaz's trust well?
qa.a: She was honest about her own failures, encouraged Dilnaz to copy her integrity rather than her habits, and pointed out Dilnaz's own strengths.
Dilnaz admires Ganga deeply as a role model, and seems surprised and touched to hear about her mistakes and her praise.

grounding: The chat shows someone whose junior looks up to and copies her, choosing honesty about her failures and modelling integrity instead of seeking adoration.

passage:
Chaitanya had worked at the Krishi Vigyan Kendra near Dharwad for three years, visiting farms on a motorbike. Binita, the new field assistant, had started copying everything: the same khaki shirt, the same way of greeting farmers, even Chaitanya's jokes.

At first Chaitanya was flattered. Then uneasy.

One afternoon, in a sugarcane field, a farmer asked a question about a new pest. Chaitanya didn't know the answer. Binita was watching.

The old Chaitanya might have bluffed. Instead: "I don't know. I'll check with the scientist at the Kendra and come back tomorrow."

On the ride back, Binita asked, "You didn't know?"

"No. And pretending would have been worse than not knowing. That farmer's crop is at stake."

Binita was quiet. "I would have made something up. I thought that's what experts do."

"That's exactly what they shouldn't do." Chaitanya smiled. "Copy that part. Not the shirt."

qa.a: At the Krishi Vigyan Kendra near Dharwad.

qa.q: What did Chaitanya feel about Binita copying everything?
qa.a: Chaitanya felt flattered at first, then uneasy about the responsibility.

qa.q: What did Chaitanya model for Binita in the sugarcane field?
qa.a: Honesty and integrity, admitting not knowing and promising to check, rather than bluffing to look like an expert.

qa.q: How does Binita see experts before this moment?
qa.a: Binita thought experts make something up rather than admit they don't know.

grounding: The passage shows someone whose junior copies their habits, feeling the honour and responsibility, and choosing to model honesty rather than seek admiration.
